rows.reason: The ForbiddenError constructor (track-read-model.ts:157) runs on every `new ForbiddenError(...)`, and a public read reaches one without touching the store. validateTrackInput checks only that sessionRefs is an array of at most 33 (track-read-model.ts:1045-1049) and never validates an entry's projectId; the activity/track route passes the body straight through (core-routes.ts:487, :1155; parseCoreRouteRequest :555-590 checks only the container). scanQueries keys the QueryRun lookup on the caller ref's sessionId only (values [goalRef.projectId, workspaceId, session.sessionId], track-read-model.ts:809-810) and pushQuery emits the bar with the asked ref itself (:820, :885; pushQuery :785-800). sessionProblemOf then sees bar.sessionRef.projectId != ctx.projectId and throws at :1068-1069, i.e. the constructor. The existing public setup tests/work-graph/S2B-30-track-bars.test.ts:333-350 builds a real QueryRun for f.computeSessionRef(); reading the same window with sessionRefs:[{projectId:'another-project', sessionId: asked.sessionId}] finds that run and returns forbidden. A second public path is the asked-Session read at :836 (a real Session created in another workspace of the same project and named by the caller). So this is a public-step gap, not tamper-only U.
rows.proposal: Keep the error type and the guard; add a public case to tests/work-graph/S2B-30-track-bars.test.ts (in the 2B-30 sessionRefs test at :333): submit/finish a real secretary Query for `asked`, then f.readTrack({ from: DAY_FROM, to: DAY_TO, sessionRefs: [{ projectId: 'another-project', sessionId: asked.sessionId }] }) and expect { status: 'rejected', code: 'forbidden' }. No store edit; the same case executes A2-053.

rows.reason: The :1078-1079 workspace arm needs a bar SessionRef that passes the project check (:1068-1069) while the Session record read at :1071-1077 has workspaceId != the Goal's workspace. Every platform writer refuses that relation: claimTask rejects a target Session of another project/workspace (claim-service.ts:997-998, and the Goal at :920); a work link's targetSession rejects another project/workspace (session-lifecycle.ts:202-213); a Query claim refuses a stored Session whose workspaceId differs from the QueryRun's workspace (query-execution.ts:890); a Session's workspaceId is fixed from the creating scope (session-directory.ts:240-245, :276). The public sessionRefs path that reaches the constructor/catch (A2-041/A2-053) throws at :1069 for a foreign projectId, or at :836 for an asked Session in another workspace, before sessionProblemOf reads any Session for :1078; a bound-project bar ref can name a Session in another workspace only when the stored record was cloned/edited, exactly the deleted test's shape. U stands.
rows.proposal: Keep the :1078-1079 workspace check untested (rule 4; T3-089's refresh says keep the production guard under R-3), or if reducing, delete only the Session read/arm at :1071-1079. Do not delete sessionProblemOf :1059-1093 wholesale as Claude proposed: its :1068-1069 project check is reachable by public sessionRefs input (A2-041/A2-053) and should get that public forbidden test, so the skeptic's objection to the bundle is right.

rows.reason: Line 1180 arm 0 is the ForbiddenError -> forbidden mapping in the catch, so any ForbiddenError thrown inside the try reaches it. The caller-supplied sessionRefs route throws one inside readTrackBarsWindow: with a real QueryRun for asked.sessionId, a foreign-project sessionRef is echoed into the turn bar by pushQuery (track-read-model.ts:820, :885) and the :1068-1069 project check throws; alternatively :836 throws for an asked Session created in another workspace of the same project. The read is inside the try (:1167-1174); :1176's CapacityError test is false and :1180's ForbiddenError test is true, so the arm returns rejected('forbidden', error.reason). That is plain public input from the activity/track route (core-routes.ts:487, :1155), no store edit, so G not U. The deleted foreign-workspace test was one tamper-only route to the same catch; it was not the only reachable route.
